verses.text: When all the kings who were beyond the Jordan, in the hill country, and in the lowland, and on all the shore of the great sea in front of Lebanon, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, heard of it
they gathered themselves together to fight with Joshua and with Israel, with one accord.
But when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai,
they also resorted to a ruse, and went and made as if they had been ambassadors, and took old sacks on their donkeys, and old, torn-up and bound up wine skins,
and old and patched shoes on their feet, and wore old garments. All the bread of their food supply was dry and moldy.
They went to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, and said to him and to the men of Israel, “We have come from a far country. Now therefore make a covenant with us.”
The men of Israel said to the Hivites, “What if you live among us. How could we make a covenant with you?”
They said to Joshua, “We are your servants.” Joshua said to them, “Who are you? Where do you come from?”
They said to him, “Your servants have come from a very far country because of the name of Yahweh your God; for we have heard of his fame, all that he did in Egypt,
and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.

Our elders and all the inhabitants of our country spoke to us, saying, ‘Take supplies in your hand for the journey, and go to meet them. Tell them, “We are your servants. Now make a covenant with us.”’
This our bread we took hot for our supplies out of our houses on the day we went out to go to you; but now, behold, it is dry, and has become moldy.
These wine skins, which we filled, were new; and behold, they are torn. These our garments and our shoes have become old because of the very long journey.”
The men sampled their provisions, and didn’t ask counsel from Yahweh’s mouth.
Joshua made peace with them, and made a covenant with them, to let them live. The princes of the congregation swore to them.
At the end of three days after they had made a covenant with them, they heard that they were their neighbors, and that they lived among them.
The children of Israel traveled and came to their cities on the third day. Now their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim.
The children of Israel didn’t strike them, because the princes of the congregation had sworn to them by Yahweh, the God of Israel. All the congregation murmured against the princes.
But all the princes said to all the congregation, “We have sworn to them by Yahweh, the God of Israel. Now therefore we may not touch them.
We will do this to them, and let them live; lest wrath be on us, because of the oath which we swore to them.”
The princes said to them, “Let them live, so they became wood cutters and drawers of water for all the congregation, as the princes had spoken to them.”
Joshua called for them, and he spoke to them, saying, “Why have you deceived us, saying, ‘We are very far from you,’ when you live among us?
Now therefore you are cursed, and some of you will never fail to be slaves, both wood cutters and drawers of water for the house of my God.”

They answered Joshua, and said, “Because your servants were certainly told how Yahweh your God commanded his servant Moses to give you all the land, and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you. Therefore we were very afraid for our lives because of you, and have done this thing.
Now, behold, we are in your hand. Do to us as it seems good and right to you to do.”
He did so to them, and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Israel, so that they didn’t kill them.
That day Joshua made them wood cutters and drawers of water for the congregation and for Yahweh’s altar to this day, in the place which he should choose.

footnotes.content: I have seen how quickly fear spreads when a people hear the Lord is moving. Here the coalition of nations knows only of Israel's conquests and wants to fight all at once, forgetting that the battle belongs to the One who goes before them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: There is a kind of unity born of panic. These kings were not of one blood or one land, yet together they resolve to resist Joshua and Israel. How often do I band together in fear when I could instead be still before the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Gibeonites were watching. They had heard of Jericho and Ai, and their hearts were not hardened to the point of blind rage like the others, but shrewd with fear. Even so, the fear of man can lead to faithlessness if not rooted in trust in the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Old sacks and patched wineskins tell a story before a word is spoken. The Gibeonites knew the power they faced, so they chose craft over courage. I must remember that our only safety is not disguise, but the mercy of the Lord Jesus who calls sinners to come as they are.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every detail of their ruse is meant to deceive. Moldy bread, patched shoes, threadbare garments. How easy it is to present a weary show to others while hiding our true need. But the Lord sees what is hidden, and He alone knows the heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They come to Gilgal, the place where Israel had rolled away reproach and renewed covenant. I find it striking that they seek covenant in the very place where the Lord had shown faithfulness to His people. Yet covenant made by deceit cannot stand before the God of truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The men of Israel are cautious for a moment. The suspicion is right, for the land was to be purged of those the Lord had marked for judgment. But caution alone is not obedience. Discernment must be joined with prayer, lest wisdom become a substitute for seeking the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A simple answer: 'We are your servants.' Words can be true in form and false in intent. I have learned to be slow to take a man at his word, but even slower to presume I need no word from the Lord before I promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They speak of the name of Yahweh with reverent lips, yet with a lying heart. How often have I seen men honor God's fame to gain what they want from His people. The fear of the Lord must be more than awe of His works, it must be love of His truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They recount the victories of Sihon and Og as distant rumors, knowing full well they are the next in line. The testimony of God's faithfulness to His people is a witness to all, yet some use it as leverage rather than bow to the God who gave it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The elders sent them with a rehearsed story and calculated supplies. There is nothing new under the sun about the schemes of fear. But no amount of preparation can cover a lie when we stand before the God who knows all things.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hot bread becomes moldy bread in their tale, a small lie made to look convincing. I am reminded that a half-truth dressed up can be more convincing than bold falsehood, and so I need humility to test what seems reasonable against the counsel of the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Torn wineskins and worn garments are proof of a long journey they never took. The world is full of props to get us what we want. But the child of God learns to rest in the truth, for in the end the Lord's justice and mercy are both sure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This is the tragedy of the whole chapter: they sampled the provisions, but did not ask counsel from Yahweh's mouth. How often have I leaned on what my eyes see and trusted my own judgment, only to find I had neglected to pray. Our greatest need is not sharper eyes, but a listening heart before the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua makes peace and a covenant in good faith. The princes swear by Yahweh, binding Israel to an oath made to deceivers. I see here the weight of a vow made in ignorance. For the believer, our word must be kept, not because our promise was wise, but because our God is faithful to His own name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three days later the truth comes to light. It is a mercy that the truth was found out, though at great cost to their discernment. I have learned that the consequences of unprayed decisions often come later, and grace to walk in them is only found by returning to the Lord who kept us despite ourselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim were not far off at all. The very places the Gibeonites feared to lose are now revealed as neighbors they had deceived. How many of our anxieties are over things we would see differently if we first sought the counsel of the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Israel does not strike them because of the oath sworn by Yahweh. The congregation murmurs, but the princes know the weight of calling on the name of the Lord. There is a godly fear here: better to keep a costly oath in reverence to God than to break it and bring guilt upon the whole people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They own the binding nature of their vow: 'We have sworn to them by Yahweh, the God of Israel.' For those who know the Lord, His name is not to be trifled with. Even in the face of their own failure, reverence for Yahweh compels them to keep their word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They choose mercy over vengeance for the sake of their oath. Wrath would come not on the deceivers first, but on Israel if they broke what they had sworn by the Lord. I am grateful that our hope rests not on keeping perfect vows, but on Jesus who has sworn Himself to keep us forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The princes spare their lives, but make them servants: woodcutters and water drawers for the congregation. What was meant to preserve life becomes a life of labor. Yet even in judgment tempered by mercy, the Lord provides a place for them among His people, a place they would not have known without grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua confronts them directly, calling out their deceit. There is no pretense, no bitterness in his question, just a fatherly reckoning of the truth. The God we serve loves both justice and truth, and He will bring both to light in His time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cursed they are to servitude, yet not cursed to destruction. Joshua's sentence is severe but restrained by the oath already made. I see a glimpse of the gospel here: we deserve to be cut off, but for the sake of the covenant the Lord has made in Jesus, our curse is taken and we are brought near to serve Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Gibeonites speak honestly at last. They feared for their lives, knowing the command of Moses to destroy the inhabitants. At least now their words are true. The fear of man drove them to deceit, but facing the truth brought them to honesty. The Lord is faithful to draw truth from a fearful heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They place themselves wholly in Joshua's hand: 'Do to us as it seems good and right to you to do.' There is resignation, but also a glimmer of trust. How blessed am I to be able to say the same to my greater Joshua, Jesus, knowing that whatever He does is good and right and merciful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua does as he said, delivering them from the hand of Israel. Mercy triumphs in the keeping of the oath. The God who binds Himself by oath will also keep us, and those who belong to Him will find that even our failures cannot undo the faithfulness of our Savior.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Woodcutters and drawers of water for the congregation and for Yahweh's altar. This humble service is precisely where the Lord places the Gibeonites, to serve at the place He would choose. I see a beautiful type of the gospel: those who once came in fear and deceit are brought to draw water for the house of God, and we who were far off have been brought near to serve our King in the true tabernacle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
